title: Binance opens Agent OS so ChatGPT, Claude Code and Cursor agents can trade; limits are left to users
summary: Binance launched Agent OS, which bundles its APIs, Wallet Agentic Hub, x402 payment facilitator API, Skill Hub and new Model Context Protocol support so that users can authorise agents in OpenAI's ChatGPT and Codex, Anthropic's Claude Code and Cursor to read market and account data and execute trades. Controls sit at the account level: agents run in dedicated subaccounts configured for specific activities such as spot or futures trading with withdrawals blocked by default, users choose between approval for every order and autonomous trading, the Agentic Wallet carries daily limits of $50,000 for swaps, $100,000 for DeFi transactions and $20 for x402 payments, but Binance sets no separate cap on how much an agent can trade or lose on the exchange beyond the amount funded into the subaccount, and its VP of product Jeff Li said the exchange cannot see the agent's reasoning and relies on the subaccount as the main line of defence if an agent is manipulated or compromised.
